title: SAF and Allied Forces Capture Hamrat al-Wiz, Tightening Control of North Kordofan Supply Corridor
detail: Sudanese army, Joint Force, and Special Task units captured the town of Hamrat al-Wiz in North Kordofan state on Sunday, September 6, 2026, driving out RSF fighters who withdrew from the area, according to military sources. Field commander Malik al-Burof said in a video filmed outside the town's captured police headquarters that 'the army, the Joint Force, and Special Task units have liberated Hamrat al-Wiz and expelled the RSF.' The town — a commercial hub for agricultural products and livestock along the highway linking North Kordofan to Khartoum — broadens the army's defensive buffer around the garrison towns of Bara and Jabrat al-Sheikh and opens routes toward Um Badr and Sodari, extending gains from the army's late-July offensive that cleared large swathes of the state and restored control of the Export Road.

title: UN Envoy Haavisto Presses Burhan, PM Idris on De-escalation and Prisoner Exchange in Khartoum Talks
detail: UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for Sudan Pekka Haavisto held a series of meetings in Khartoum on Sunday, September 6, 2026 with Sovereignty Council chairman and army chief Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Prime Minister Kamil Idris, and Finance Minister/JEM leader Jibril Ibrahim, conveying 'important messages regarding de-escalation and the protection of civilians' and saying 'dialogue is the path to achieving sustainable peace and a comprehensive ceasefire.' Haavisto said he looked forward to continuing meetings toward an exchange of prisoners and civilian detainees in cooperation with the ICRC. Sudanese officials stressed national sovereignty; Jibril Ibrahim rejected proposals to expand the Darfur arms embargo to all of Sudan as a violation of sovereignty. A Quintet delegation (African Union, EU, IGAD, Arab League, UN) was expected in Khartoum on September 8 for follow-on political consultations.
